title: FOOLS WILL RESIGN!!
summary: Walk away from repeated checks, then sacrifice the knight to change the rook’s checking file.

nodes.question: Which king reply keeps the promotion plan alive?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Rc1+: White has Kf1/Rh1/Nh7/e6 against Kb6/Rc1/f6. The earlier eight-piece d-pawn capture remains source context.

branches.title: Change the checking file with a knight sacrifice
commentary: Begin in the complete seven-piece diagram after ...Rc1+. The selected king walk changes what the rook can do after checking.
Kf2 keeps the king near the e-file instead of abandoning the pawn.
Rxh1 takes White’s rook, but spends the checking tempo.
e7 puts the pawn one step from promotion.
Rh2+ begins the sequence of rank checks.
Kf3 keeps the king near e2/e3, cutting off a direct rook return.
Rh3+ checks again.
Kf4 climbs while preserving the pawn threat.
Rh4+ keeps checking along the rank.
Kf5 continues toward f6.
Rh5+ checks once more.
Kxf6 removes Black’s f-pawn.
Rh6+ reaches the critical point: climbing farther would lose the knight with check.
Kf5 retreats rather than permitting ...Rxh7+.
Rh5+ follows with check.
Kf4 continues down until a route to the other side opens.
Rh4+ keeps the king under attack.
Ke3 changes sides of the e-file, preparing a different king shelter.
Rh3+ continues the checks.
Kd4 steps to the queenside of the pawn.
Rh4+ checks on the fourth rank.
Kd5 climbs again from the other side.
Rh5+ follows the king.
Kd6 prepares the knight interposition.
Rh6+ checks, but this time White has Nf6.
Nf6 blocks the rook check and offers the knight, forcing a change of checking file in the selected capture.
Rxf6+ removes the knight and moves the rook from h6 to f6.
Kd5 retreats again; rushing upward would restore a skewer or blockade.
Rf5+ follows on the newly chosen file.
Kd4 keeps heading toward e2.
Rf4+ checks along the fourth rank.
Kd3 steps toward the final shelter.
Rf3+ gives another check.
Ke2 reaches the safe square. The rook can no longer recreate the previous h-file blockade.
Rf5 is the illustrated waiting move at the end of the source sequence.
e8=Q is an independently checked promotion completion. The resulting queen-versus-rook ending is winning, requiring conversion rather than immediate mate.

branches.title: Retreat away from the e-file
commentary: Compare the source’s drawing king retreat and rook exchange.
Kg2 gives up the forced win by moving too far from the e-file.
Rxh1 takes White’s rook, but White can now recapture that rook with its king.
Kxh1 removes Black’s rook and leaves the king far from the advanced e-pawn.
Kc6 approaches the pawn before White’s knight can support it.
e7 still threatens promotion, but this exact knight-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play. The rook has disappeared from both sides.

branches.title: Continue upward at the critical check
commentary: Follow the initial winning route, then test the source’s tempting upward king move.
Kf2 keeps the pawn plan alive.
Rxh1 captures the rook.
e7 threatens promotion.
Rh2+ starts the checks.
Kf3 approaches the checking rook’s line.
Rh3+ checks again.
Kf4 climbs toward the advanced f-pawn.
Rh4+ continues checking.
Kf5 approaches the black pawn.
Rh5+ checks once more.
Kxf6 removes f6.
Rh6+ reaches the critical choice.
Kf7 gives up the win because the knight can be captured with check.
Rxh7+ removes the knight while keeping the king busy. The exact rook-versus-pawn ending is drawn with best play.

exercises.answer: After ...Rxf6+, the rook checks from the f-file. White can retreat to e2 without letting it return to the old h-file blockade.
